title: Paise Add
statement: Implement `solve(a_rupee, a_paise, b_rupee, b_paise)`. Convert each rupee-paise pair to paise (100 paise in a rupee) and return the sum as an integer number of paise. Do not use binary floats. Inputs are integers and paise may be 100 or more.
constraints: Return total paise, not a rupee pair
starter_code:
def solve(a_rupee, a_paise, b_rupee, b_paise):
    pass
hints: Multiply rupees by 100 and add the paise.
Do the same for both amounts, then add.
There is no carry step to write if the unit is already paise.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: Money in this course is an integer of minor units.

editorial: Money in this course is an integer of minor units. Adding rupees in float introduces binary dust. Converting both amounts to paise first makes the sum exact and makes a later carry, if you ever need a rupee display, a separate formatting step.
reference_solution:
def solve(a_rupee, a_paise, b_rupee, b_paise):
    return (a_rupee * 100 + a_paise) + (b_rupee * 100 + b_paise)
